title: Test failures on ppc64le
body:
- Neo4j version: 5.5.0
- Operating system: Ubuntu 22.04
- API/Driver: Java 17
- **Steps to reproduce**
1. Build neo4j on ppc64le
- Expected behavior
- The build and tests pass.
- Actual behavior
Build is successful but tests are failing.

Hi Team,
We are trying to build and test neo4j on IBM ppc64le processor architecture and observing some test failures, indicating it may not be supported. Upon analysing the failed tests we found that the page size in the neo4j code has been hardcoded to 8K at some places. The system page size on ppc64le is 65K. We even tried to fix the test failures by patching the code, but that results in some more failures in other sub-projects even if it fixes the original ones. Can you consider fixing the code so it is platform independent?
Thank you.
cc: @participant4

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Hi @reporter ,
as you have correctly guessed we don't support ppc64. We generally develop and test only for the platforms listed here https://neo4j.com/docs/operations-manual/current/installation/requirements/#deployment-requirements-platforms .
We have recently introduced support for ARM and the quality assurance part of the project was considerable amount of work, so I am pretty sure there are no plans to support additional architectures like ppc64 in the near future.
The hardcoded 8K pages are pieces of memory used for caching. In database terminology, they are usually called buffer cache pages. The have nothing to do with OS or processor pages. For instance, Postgresql uses 8k and Mysql 16k. I expect the problems are in other places that the 8k buffer cache page.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
@participant1 Four tests are failing for us (will have to confirm their names):

```
countNotModifiedPagesPerChunkWithNoBuffers()
countFlushesPerChunkWithNoBuffers()
countMergesPerChunkWithNoBuffers()
countUsedBuffersPerChunkWithNoBuffers()

```
They are all failing because the offset being used in inside flushAndForce() is 8192. If its changed to 65536, they pass.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: @reporter Ok. I will check if there is something platform-specific about those tests

comments.author: participant1

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
@participant1 

https://github.com/neo4j/neo4j/blob/5ad4387ed521f169a737f9836402dbac8759a9fc/community/community-it/community-it/src/test/java/org/neo4j/io/pagecache/impl/muninn/MuninnPageCacheTest.java#L950

https://github.com/neo4j/neo4j/blob/5ad4387ed521f169a737f9836402dbac8759a9fc/community/io/src/main/java/org/neo4j/io/pagecache/impl/muninn/MuninnPagedFile.java#L590

I changed filePageSize to 65536 only inside this function, and the failing tests passed. Didn't run the entire suite.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
@reporter OK, so there is nothing really hardcoded in MuninnPagedFile, is there?
What the test https://github.com/neo4j/neo4j/blob/5ad4387ed521f169a737f9836402dbac8759a9fc/community/community-it/community-it/src/test/java/org/neo4j/io/pagecache/impl/muninn/MuninnPageCacheTest.java#L950
does is just adding a file to the page cache and telling it to use 8K logical pages to do caching and IO. This is processor architecture independent thing. As I wrote above it is the same concept as Postgresql using 8k and Mysql 16k for the same purpose.
I think there is another issue and the test passing with 64K is just a coincidence.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Maybe there is really something ppc64 incompatible in the page cache, but changing the test to use 64K for caching will most likely be just masking the problem. And since all our deployments use 8K pages, we prefer keeping 8k in our tests.
